items.item_text: High school diploma and/or relevant experience working in a testing center.
Experience working independently and as a team member exercising independent good judgment, problem-solving and decision-making skills in consultation with team members as appropriate.
Four years’ experience working within higher education/academic setting.
Experience providing complex administrative support in a Director-level office environment.
Extensive experience with student accommodation process, procedures, and services for students with disabilities.
Experience handling difficult, sensitive, and/or confidential information.
Experience developing policy recommendations to department management.
Knowledge and experience with a variety of computer programs including Microsoft Office Suite, electronic scheduling, electronic mail, and web tools.

Under the general direction of SDC/AES Supervisor(s), coordinates student exams and administrative Accommodated Exam Services (AES) functions. In the absence of the Supervisor, oversees unit operations and serves as the lead to AES professional staff, supervises approximately 60 student workers. Manages sensitive disability and accommodation information, ensures exam security, communicates diplomatically with diverse groups such as students, faculty, staff, and administrators. Coordinate and schedules testing appointments (appx 26,000 annually) verifying that accommodation requirements are met. Maintain confidentiality and discretion in all areas. Manage and direct client/community traﬃc and inquiries. Creates and maintain essential conﬁdential electronic and paper records ensuring accuracy and exam integrity.

Interpersonal and communication skills to tactfully and diplomatically engage with a diverse community including students with disabilities, faculty, staff, parents, prospective students, and others to provide excellent customer service.
Ability to work with frequent interruptions in a high paced, student-centered environment and multitask and prioritize multiple demands and requests.
Organizational skills to set goals, plan and prioritize workload; and to manage several ongoing projects simultaneously in a complex work environment.
Knowledge of and ability to interpret and apply SDC departmental and university policy and procedures and applicable federal laws for providing academic accommodations to students with disabilities.
Leadership/training skills to run/modify a structured training program aimed towards student staff and especially new student staff hires.
